_meta.why: our mainnet tier paints our own generator's liquidity over real topology, and that generator is the one the evolved routers' priors were fit to. This is the first liquidity family in the program we did not author.

Q1_does_the_ordering_survive.answer: YES, decisively, and the margin is WIDER than on the tier whose balances we drew ourselves.
Q1_does_the_ordering_survive.magnitude: on the classic mainnet tier lnd scores 0.694 and the champions 0.790, a gap of 0.097. Here lnd scores 0.596 and the champions 0.723-0.728, a gap of 0.127-0.132. The whole tier is harder for everyone, and the paradigm's edge GREW by about a third rather than shrinking.
Q1_does_the_ordering_survive.every_comparison_is_10_0: all six arms beat lnd on all ten files, sign p = .002, every CI excluding zero.
Q1_does_the_ordering_survive.consistency_check: atomic1 is the top arm here at 0.728. exp-017 identified it as the FLAT-liquidity specialist (ladder rank 4 to 1 monotone as liquidity flattens), and this graph is a soft U-shape with 32.7% of channels in the sub-5/over-95 tails against roughly 63% for our bimodal generator. An independent balance sheet placing atomic1 first is the specialist story predicting a result on data it was never shown.

Q2_does_ilnd_track_the_champions.answer: YES. Statistically indistinguishable from all three, and CI-solidly ahead of lnd.

production_default.note: the same from_graph files at 50,000 ppm, which is what lnrpc.CalculateFeeLimit gives a caller who sets no limit. Every payment here is 100,000 sat or larger, far above the 1,000 sat cut-off, so the injection is production's own number.
production_default.reading: ilnd GAINS 0.0038 under the production budget while paying 267 fewer ppm; lnd and mx_c3 are unmoved. fee_limit_failures is 0.0 per file for all three arms, reproducing round 6's finding that the production default is too loose to separate anyone on budget discipline.

Q3_balance_family_versus_topology.answer: The balance FAMILY is worth very little, and what it is worth it gives to everyone roughly equally. Essentially the whole score is topology plus the paradigm.
Q3_balance_family_versus_topology.reading: the foreign balance sheet is slightly EASIER than our own bimodal generator for every arm, by 0.009 to 0.025 of objective. Not one of the seven CIs excludes zero, and the spread between arms is smaller than any single arm's interval. Critically the deltas do NOT favour the routers whose priors were fit to our generator: mx_c3 has the SMALLEST gain (+0.009) and the never-fitted seed among the largest (+0.025).
Q3_balance_family_versus_topology.why_that_answers_the_circularity_caveat: if the champions' scores were an artifact of being fit to sim_liquidity.go's ExpFloat64()*0.05 draw, moving to a balance sheet drawn by someone else's model should have cost them relative to lnd and to the seed. It cost them nothing; the lnd gap grew.

source_rebalance_control.reading: restoring the sealed tier's 50/50 rebalance of the source's own channels costs every arm 0.008 to 0.011, in the same direction and the same size, so the variant-A choice to leave the source unbalanced is not carrying any of the result.

Q4_the_fee_liquidity_signal.literal_question: does any arm's per-file score correlate with how much fee-signal its routes could have exploited?
Q4_the_fee_liquidity_signal.status: NOT CLEANLY MEASURABLE AS ASKED, and not forced. Scoring 'fee-signal its routes could have exploited' needs a per-route counterfactual: the signal an arm DID use against the signal available on the routes it did not take. Nothing in the aggregate output carries that, and reconstructing it from traces would be a per-attempt attribution model whose assumptions would drive the answer.

the_signal_exists.reading: real but modest, and in the intuitive direction: a node charging more has less of its own liquidity. Worth about 0.08 of balance fraction between the fee extremes.

what_is_measurable_and_was_measured.a_well_posed_substitute: if that correlation were exploitable, arms that price fees should gain MORE on variant A, where the correlation exists, than on variant B, where our generator draws balances independently of fees. That is exactly the Q3 A-minus-B delta, already computed per arm.
what_is_measurable_and_was_measured.result: NO EVIDENCE of exploitation. The ranking of A-minus-B gains is seed +0.025, econ2 +0.023, lnd +0.020, atomic1 +0.016, hb1 +0.015, ilnd +0.012, mx_c3 +0.009. econ2, the only router that reads fee budgets, sits second but is bracketed by the never-fitted seed above it and stock lnd below it, and no CI excludes zero. The ordering does not track fee-awareness.

verdict.headline: The de-circularization holds. On a balance sheet generated by someone else's model, every evolved router and the interval port beat stock lnd on all ten files with p = .002, by 0.105 to 0.132 of objective against the 0.097 the classic mainnet tier shows -- the edge is wider, not narrower, on liquidity nobody here fit to. Swapping our own generator in on the identical topology moves every arm by less than 0.026 and nobody significantly, and it moves the fitted champions LESS than the never-fitted seed. The interval router tracks the champions exactly (-0.001 vs mx_c3, CI straddling zero) and gains slightly under production's own fee default.
